see.b: A cultural centre with gallery, movie theatre, video room, library and stages; usually hosts the main exhibitions in town. An interesting building completed in 1906 with old-fashioned elevators/lifts.
French cultural centre built in 1820, with gallery and video hall.
Hosts the city council.
Colonial structure built in 1750 that brought water from springs to downtown.
City Theatre, inspired by the Paris Opéra House.

The National Library offers guided tours on weekdays, showing visitors its rare collection, various bookstacks and the catalogue system. Registration with identification is required, and tours run for about an hour. They leave at 13:00…

see.a: Rua Texeira de Freitas at Rua Mestre Valentim
see.b: Commissioned in 1779, this was to become the first public park in the Americas. Check out the original Rococo-style gate and the ironwork fountains.
The headquarters for the federal gas (petrol) company is an interesting piece of brutalist architecture which somehow resembles a Rubik's Cube with some blocks missing.
Large park; good for a rest. Look for monkeys and capybaras that roam about.

see.a: Rua Marquês de Sapucaí - Praça Onze
see.b: Site of the famous Carnaval parades, the Sambódromo is a long street flanked by grandstands and VIP boxes. From the start of the year until Carnaval week, technical rehearsals (Ensaios Técnicos) free to the public are held on…
A stairway covered by colorful tiles and the ever-evolving art work of Chilean artist Jorge Selarón.

see.n: Estátua equestre de D. Pedro I

see.b: A beautiful spot for a stroll along the bank of Guanabara Bay.

see.b: The place where, during the first decades of the 19th century, ships carrying a total of almost a million African slaves landed. When slave trade was banned, freed slaves lived there for some time, eventually the whole area was entirely…
It is near the site where Brazil was declared a Republic in 1889. It's also the site of the monument for Republican leader Benjamin Constant.

Small but interesting church built in 1739. It is more correctly known as the Outeira da Gloria, outeira in Portuguese meaning “knoll” or small hill. The church was well sited to be seen by arriving sailors sailing into Guanabara Bay.…

see.n: Benedictine Monastery of Rio de Janeiro
see.b: Colonial architecture. Founded in 1590.
Neoclassic cathedral.
A rather bizarre, modern cathedral shaped like a volcano, with a very impressively vacuous interior.

These churches were built in the 18th century as part of a Carmelite Convent. After the future Portuguese King John VI of Portugal arrived in Rio in 1808 the churches became the city’s former main cathedral and the royal chapel. It was…
Colonial church built in 1773.
Baroque

see.n: Church Our Lady of La Salette
see.b: Founded in 1914. It has neo Gothic arches. One of the most beautiful church in Rio de Janeiro.

see.n: Museum of the Estate of Ceu
see.h: Daily except Tue 12:00-17:00; closed for major holidays
see.b: An art and antique museum with a good collection of works by modern masters. During Carnaval 2006 some of its most famous works of art were stolen while a procession passed by outside.
For researchers about the Brazilian film, radio, and broadcasting industries.
After MASP in São Paulo, the second most important contemporary art museum in Brazil, (downtown, next to Santos Dumont airport). Modernist architecture on the edge of the Bay.
A museum of Brazilian history stretching from colonial to imperial times; big collection of paintings, but poor in artifacts.
Installed in a building constructed in 1868, this museum preserves articles from the seafaring history of the city.
Another building modelled on one in Paris, this time the Louvre. Includes large paintings from Academicist and Neoclassical Brazilian artists, as well as many copies of European sculptures

A museum opened in 2013 as part of the regeneration of the old port area. Made up of a new building with good views from the roof, next to a converted building that had been part of Rio’s former bus station. Rotating exhibitions…
This small tram museum has photos of and artifacts from the glory days when trams were all over Rio, including some models of old tramcars and lots of electrical equipment.

see.pr: R$30 adults, R$15 youth under 21, free for seniors 60+ or children under 6
see.b: Forward-looking science museum in a compact but stunning Santiago Calatrava-designed building.

Learn about the history of Brazil's military as you stroll through galleries with exhibits about historic conflicts and leaders. Large collection of military hardware including tanks, field artillery, and rocket launchers.
Former ministry of culture, designed by French architect Le Corbusier; though small, it is regarded as an important pioneering work in modern architecture.
The former Customs House for Rio has some fascinating decorations and is well worth the visit.
Former presidential palace (1889-1893) and foreign office; now hosts a museum of South American diplomacy, a library and the UN information offices in Brazil.
Old Imperial Palace built in 1743 (though impressively modest). Colonial architecture.

The seat of the Legislative Assembly, visitors are welcome to wander in the corridors along the perimeter of the first floor, which tell the history of the Legislative Assembly and the building (mostly in Portuguese). Access to the…
Held over a few days in May and November of each year, when Santa Teresa's artists open their studios to the public. There are free shuttle buses from most parts of the city for this event.

see.a: Rua Júlio do Carmo, 251 - Cidade Nova

see.b: This arts and entertainment complex celebrates Carnaval year-round. Thursday nights at 20:00, there is a special Carnaval samba presentation called Forces of Nature (Forças da Natureza), which includes a dinner buffet, for R$190 per…

What was Brazil's only remaining metropolitan tramway, in continuous operation since 1859, ran from Largo da Carioca, across the Arcos da Lapa, and into Santa Teresa terminating at the Largo de Curvelo. The tramway was closed in 2014…
A good place to catch free classical music concerts. Stop by during the day for a schedule or check the newspaper for events, as the surrounding neighborhood can be a bit shady at night.

see.a: Av. Presidente Castelo Branco at Av. Maracanã
see.b: Once the world's highest capacity football venue, it was able to hold nearly 200,000 people. In modern times, the capacity has been reduced because of safety considerations, and the introduction of seating for all fans. It is undergoing…

see.b: A few km north of the beach, this mountainous subtropical forest is Brazil's smallest national park. It is largely hand-planted as much of the original forest was destroyed to make way for coffee plantations. Despite this it contains…

see.a: Rua Arquias Cordeiro - Engenho de Dentro
see.b: Estádio Olímpico João Havelange, known by its nickname of Engenhão, is a new soccer stadium built for the Pan-American Games of 2007. A modern construction, not as big as Maracanã but still worth a visit for soccer fans. The Botafogo…

This 55-hectare park preserves some of the original forest and serves as a refuge for a wide range of species including marmosets, bush dogs, guinea pigs, parakeets, vultures, and hawks. The park includes the Pedra do Andaraí, symbol of…

see.n: Museum of Astronomy and Related Sciences
see.b: Also has an observatory.
A museum about the reign of Emperor Pedro I (1822-1831), but with a modest collection.

The mosaic sidewalks along Boulevard 28 de Setembro between Praça Maracanã and Praça Barão de Drummond are musical staves. Written in the stones are 20 complete musical works, including tunes by Ary Barroso, Martinho da Vila, Almirante,…

see.a: Parque Quinta da Boa Vista - São Cristóvão
see.b: If you won't be making it to the Amazon or the Pantanal, this is a good place to see some of Brazil's more exotic creatures.

see.a: Rua Arquias Cordeiro 1046 - Engenho de Dentro
see.b: A modest collection of 19th-century engines, train cars used by emperors and presidents, and streetcars.

see.a: Estrada do Açude, 764 - Alto da Boa Vista
see.b: The former residence of one of the founders of the Modern Art Museum, this museum hosts a collection of items from the history of Portuguese rule, including furniture, kitchenware, and an array of azulejos, or Portuguese blue tiles.…

see.b: Many climbers take on the 444-meter Pedra do Andaraí, in Grajaú State Park. See the See section for details.

eat.b: Quick and quiet spot for a light lunch.
A good place to try the Brazilian take on Middle Eastern food.
Dates back to 1894 and has a dazzling tea room and arguably the best sweets and other delicacies in town.
Delivery service. - Other units: Avenida Ataulfo de Paiva, 1228 - Leblon. (+55 21 2294-0797), - Avenida Armando Lombardi, 75, Loja A - Barra da Tijuca, (+55 21 3153-4040).
Buffet and cafe of salads, different meats, and desserts.
Try the house specialty of mutton with rice and broccoli (carneiro com arroz com brócolis).
Another weigh & pay buffet that includes sushi.
Has some of the freshest fish in Rio. Go on Monday, Wednesday or Friday, when they have live samba and chorinho music by renowned artists. Try their moqueca dishes. Air Conditioning.
Come here for some comfort Brazilian food, little fritters and feijoada and a Brahma to wash it down.
This restaurante mineiro, inside an antique villa, has nice veranda and garden seating with great views of Guanabara Bay. Reservations recommended.

Another fine restaurant in an old villa built in the 1930s, this eatery serves exotic dishes from the Amazon region, including fish such as piranha, and unusual fruits like cupuaçu, taperabá, and jambu. They also have a good selection…

A beautifully restored former grocery store, with a high ceiling, nice wooden furnishings, and beer that's always ice-cold. Located a bit past where most tourists get off the tram, and frequented by an eclectic local crowd which spills…

eat.a: Rua Pascoal Carlos Magno, 115 - Santa Teresa
eat.b: Lively and popular with the young crowd. And not simply a bar; the food is inexpensive but good.

This is in fact not a club but a street party. This place was a quite small and hidden beer and beverage deposit store. After a change in the administration it changed into a bar, offering good quality live music, and turned into one of…
Pleasant little place for a drink or two, with a view of Praça Neves with the tram line. If you get hungry, try the pizza.

Located in a nice old house from the 1900s, this place always has good samba groups playing. One of the best days is on Monday nights when on stage you can see one of the most powerful voices of samba, the singer Richah, with his group…
Live music venue with plenty of live Carioca music.

Clube dos Democráticos was founded in 1867 and is one of the first carnaval groups of Rio. Nowadays the great ballroom of the beginning of the 20th century houses one of the best places to dance Brazilian rhythms, especially samba, in…

One of the most beautiful and best-known samba clubs in Rio de Janeiro. Was once elected by the British newspaper The Guardian as being one of the top 10 bars in the world. Nice decor, filled with antiques, paintings, medieval armors,…
Dance club.
As the name suggests they are best at carne-de-sol. They have a full menu of typical Brazilian food in good-sized helpings.
This hole-in-the-wall joint has fantastic food that has attracted fans for over four decades. Lamb with vegetables and potatoes is a must-try.
Good-quality Italian restaurant with reasonable prices. Note that they do not accept credit cards.

This restaurant has for decades been the haunt of famous bohemian composers and poets such as Noel Rosa and Martinho da Vila. It remains the hotspot of Vila Isabel, with daily buffets, and feijoada on Saturdays. It also holds the…
Fine dining in what used to be the chapel for the Imperial Palace. The food is a fantastic display of traditional Brazilian cuisine with formal service.
Famous for its shrimp risotto and empadinhas. Delivery available. Accepts credit cards.
Gay and lesbian nightclub.

Pepe was a famous hang glider who passed away in a hang gliding accident in Japan a few years ago. He started a sandwich shop on the beach that makes a variety of healthy sandwiches. Especially good are the fruit smoothies. Not to be…
Alpendre's menu is full of typical Brazilian cuisine from around the country.

eat.a: Avenida das Americas 1600 - Barra da Tijuca
eat.b: Although unexpected it is delightful. Germany food in Rio! Fantastic breakfast and salad bar.
Excellent vegan option with three-course meals in a more lush quarter of Recreio. Offers pizza delivery on Saturdays. Prices can be a bit steep for locals.

eat.a: Avenida Ayrton Senna 2541 - Barra da Tijuca
eat.b: This churrascaria has unusually excellent meat and shrimp along with a salad bar and all the other standards of the genre. There is a monitored play area for children.
Bar with a varied schedule of live music from Monday to Saturday, covering all types of music, from jazz to choro.

eat.h: closes only with the sun raising
eat.b: The menu is composed by big sandwiches, with whatever you want: ham, salami, cheese, tenderloin and so on, with one home special ingredient: a big pineapple slice. It's a tropical taste to the end of your night. Famous for making their…
This two-story shopping arcade has a number of inexpensive Middle Eastern restaurants on the ground floor.
Some fine Parisian cuts here, roast duck, whatever you like.
Seafood restaurant with good selection.
Italian cuisine.
Serves nothing but traditional, authentic Brazilian feijoada.
A good alternative to churrascarias, this steakhouse is simple and cozy. During the weekends there are usually big lines, but the steak is delicious. Try Filé à Oswaldo Aranha, with toasted garlic.
A trendy restaurant with excellent salads, main dishes and desserts.
Good-value rodizio – all-you-can-eat salad and barbecue.
Fairly authentic and very popular Thai restaurant. Reservations essential at weekends.
A good per-kilo restaurant. It is attached to a whole foods shop and has a good buffet selection, including sushi.
This grill restaurant offers a great bang for the buck: from their veranda you get to people-watch pretty Brazilians. There you can enjoy tasty wraps and sandwiches.
Sushi.
One of the best churrascaria in town.

eat.a: Av. Nossa Senhora de Copacabana, 796 - Copacabana
eat.b: Very good all-you-can-eat rodizio.
A trendy, sexy and exotic place with great South Asian dishes. Good to go as a couple.
With over 500 varieties, this is the place to start your studies of Brazil's national drink.

This unpretentious and thoroughly un-touristy hole-in-the-wall botequim has been a favorite hang-out of top local musicians for decades and hosts regular live choro, samba, and bossanova performances.

Popular with the younger crowd, that hangs out there to listen to DJs playing rock. Most of the crowd hangs out there because they are underage and can't get in the underground nightclubs. Gets packed with foreigners during summer.

eat.a: Rua Vinicius de Moraes and Rua Prudente de Morais - Ipanema
eat.b: There's no better place in Rio, Brazil, or even the world to watch bathing beauties stroll by than this cafe-bar, named after the song which according to legend was written here in 1962.
Pizza and draft beer is the name of the game here, though good quality. And save room for dulce de leche.
Nightclub.

"Fosfo" as it's nicknamed by the goers has a strong Saturday rock-oriented party. Young, trendy crowd with djs playing mostly indie rock, discopunk and electro-rock. After 04:00 it has a more electronic after-party. Different parties…

A fairly new establishment, offering a bit of Lapa in the Zona Sul. Live music (samba, choro, MPB) Tu-Su. They seem to have a knack for booking the lesser-known offspring and siblings of more famous musicians.
Hosts lesser names, mainly performing Brazilian music.
The city's main venue for classical performances.
